texts: My uncle never spent a rupee on himself and kept adding to his bank balance until the day he was gone, and now his sons are quarrelling over it.
doha on a miser piling up money he cant take with him pls
Pile it high, O miser, heap upon heap, for the heap will stay behind when you walk out empty-handed.

Please write a doha about the man who spends his whole life piling up savings and property, refusing joy and generosity, and who leaves everything behind exactly as it was, with nothing in his hands at the end.
miser's hoard, left behind

I have spent thirty years buying land and building up deposits, always saying one more year, one more property, and I'm starting to wonder what all of it is for. Write a doha for me about hoarding wealth.
riches left behind
Mountains of coin are counted in the quiet night, and at dawn the counter departs with nothing but his name.
My landlord checks his rents every evening with a trembling finger and will not repair the roof, because the money must never be touched.
need a doha about people who collect riches and take none of it along
the miser's heap
At my grandfather's reading of the will, the family discovered bundles of cash hidden in every cupboard, never used, never enjoyed, and everyone just stood there quiet.
Compose a doha about a rich man who guards his fortune so tightly that he never eats properly, never helps anyone, and in the end it all passes to strangers who did nothing to earn it.
doha about hoarding property, all gone at the end anyway
The heap of riches grows tall, but a pile of wealth is a poor comfort for the final sleep.
The sun rises on the rich man's lands and sets on them, and the cuckoo sings on, indifferent to what he owns and will soon leave.
My neighbour counted his farmland acre by acre each morning while the cuckoo called from the mango branch, and his children are selling it all already.
doha pls, cuckoo singing while a rich man counts his property under the sun
sun, cuckoo, rich man's property

Please write a doha where the sun and the cuckoo go on with their day, untouched by the hoarder's anxious counting of land and savings, to show that his heap will fall away while the world carries on.
touchstone, leaf, miser's wealth
doha on a touchstone and a leaf, how piles of riches fall away at the end
The jeweller tested my father's old ring on a touchstone, and I found a dried leaf in the same drawer, and suddenly his whole lifetime of saving seemed so small.
The touchstone tests the heap and finds it brittle as a dry leaf, and the wind of time lifts it from the hoarder's hand.
Write a doha where a touchstone reveals the true worth of a hoarded fortune and it turns out as light as a fallen leaf, to remind us that riches saved up for a lifetime do not stay with us.
The sword guards the vault, the vault holds the heap, and the heap holds no lasting thing at all.
write a doha about a rich man hiring guards with swords to protect savings he'll leave behind anyway
The old zamindar down our lane keeps a sword by his bed to guard his property, but his heirs are already circling like they can't wait.
sword, hoarded riches
Please compose a doha showing a man who guards his piles of wealth with a sword all his life, sleeping badly and trusting no one, and in the end the sword protects none of it from slipping away.
tongue, miser's wealth
doha about someone who talks big with their tongue about their riches but cant keep any
My uncle's tongue was always busy bragging about his land and bank deposits, and now that he's gone, all that bragging has left nothing for anyone to hold.

Write a doha about the tongue that boasts of acres and savings with endless pride, though everything that is boasted about will be left behind, and only the sound of the boasting remains to remind others of vanity.
The tongue sings of fortunes piled high, yet the fortune and the singer both fall silent in the end.
In our old family court case over the inheritance, the lawyers' fees ate up half the property, while my aunt kept a lotus in a bowl and a lamp lit in prayer and told us it wasn't worth it.
doha on a lotus and a lamp vs the rich mans heap of property
lotus, lamp, hoarded riches

Please write a doha where a lotus floats serene and a lamp burns quietly, contrasted with the rich man who piles up property and savings all his life only to leave them behind without a moment of peace.
The lotus asks for nothing and the lamp gives all it has, while the rich man hoards to the last breath and loses it all.
shroud, lock, hoarded riches
Dad fitted a heavy lock on the cabinet holding his savings, and at the end he was wrapped in a plain white shroud with nothing in his hands but the keys.
doha with a shroud and a lock, about riches you cant take with you
Lock after lock he fastened on his fortune, and in the end only a shroud with no pockets was his.
Write a doha about the miser who fits lock upon lock to guard his wealth, only to be wrapped at last in a plain shroud that has no place for a single coin, leaving all his hoarded heap behind.
The crow caws from the miser's wall while his heirs count what he guarded, for the heap outlived the hoarder.
crow, miser's heap
A crow perches on the wall of a great estate that its owner spent his life adding to, and the crow carries off a crumb while the owner carries nothing. Please write a doha about this contrast.
A crow sat on my father's gate on the day we opened his safe, and the neat piles of notes he had saved all those years suddenly meant nothing to any of us.
doha with a crow and a rich mans pile of money he left behind pls
Please write me a doha about a family friend who built an empire of flats and offices and never took a day off, and who now lies in a hospital bed unable to touch any of it.
Heaped riches will not follow their lord into the dark, for the dark asks for no deposit.
wealth that stays behind
doha about piling up property and leaving it all
My boss works twenty hours a day to expand his holdings and says he'll rest later, though his doctor warns that later may not come.
miser, fortune, nothing carried
can u write a doha for someone who keeps hoarding savings and wont enjoy any
Compose a doha on how the one who hoards a huge stack of savings and refuses to give a handful to anyone in need ends by leaving it all to people who never loved him for it.
Ah, the hoarder's heart is a locked and silent place, and when he leaves, all he guarded is simply sold.
My neighbour wears the same coat for ten years yet owns four plots of land, and I don't think he has smiled once in all that time.

The prayer beads slip through the old man's fingers as he counts, but his mind counts his savings and the milk he sells each morning, and nothing of that count will go with him. Please write a doha about this.
prayer beads, milk, hoarded riches
He tells his beads at dawn and counts his coins at dusk, and the milk of kindness never flows from his closed hand.
doha pls, prayer beads and milk, about a rich guy hoarding money while praying
Our dairy owner prays with prayer beads every morning, then waters down the milk to stack away extra savings, and I wonder what he thinks he'll keep.
doha about people who hoard riches and lose it all to others at the end
I would like a doha that shows the sad comedy of a man who spends every moment multiplying his property and bank balance, but who has no time to enjoy any of it and leaves it to be squabbled over.
How the hoarder labours to fill what cannot be filled, and calls his weariness a fortune.
My cousin sold his ancestral home and every heirloom to build up his business holdings, and he now sits alone in a big empty office doing nothing with them.
heaps of wealth, soon gone
doha with a house in it, about a rich man whose big property is left behind
He built a great mansion of marble and ivory, and it outlived him by a hundred years, with a stranger asleep in his bed.

Please write a doha about a man who spent his life adding rooms and floors to his house, collecting property after property, and who in the end walks out of its gates alone without carrying a single brick.
My great-uncle's house has twelve rooms and he lived in one, guarding the rest like treasure, and now the rest is just dust and arguments.
house, hoarded riches
A skeleton lies where the rich man's silk once lay, and the fortune he heaped now belongs to the one who counts it next.
skeleton, hoarded fortune

Write a doha where a skeleton rests inside the great mansion that its owner spent a lifetime filling with wealth, showing that the hoarded heap has fallen away from the bones while the bones lie empty.
Walking by the old family mansion, I noticed the owner's portrait, still stern about his savings, and I thought of a skeleton in a fine suit guarding his money.
doha with a skeleton and a miser, riches left behind
doha about a net spread to catch more and more money, but it all slips away
He cast his net over the crowd of men, hauling in rupee after rupee, until the net itself tore and the haul was lost.
A man casts a wide net to gather riches from every side, never satisfied, but at the end the net tears and the catch spills back, leaving him empty-handed. Write a doha on this.
net, hoarded riches
My brother keeps casting a net of side businesses and investments to catch more and more, and his health has been the only thing slipping through.
The priest at our local shrine always asks for donations yet is said to sleep on bars of yellow metal; he has built a fortune from people's offerings and keeps it all.
priest, hoarded riches
doha about a priest who hoards money from the faithful, and loses it all at the end
Please write a doha for the priest who collects offerings and turns them into a private fortune, forgetting that the heap he guards will fall away from him at the last, as it does for every hoarder.
The priest chants of the beyond while his hands hold fast to heaps of this world's fortune, and the heap slips as the chant ends.
Heaped and heaped, the riches grow; scattered and scattered, they will be, when the hoarder has been taken from them.
what the miser leaves
doha on someone who keeps gathering property and cant stop
At the hospital, my uncle was still on the phone about a land deal, and the nurses were already preparing the paperwork for his departure.

Compose a doha on the endless gathering of money and land by a person who believes that having more will protect him from every sorrow, yet who cannot take a single coin of it beyond the end of his days.
A beggar sat outside the rich man's gate with a bright mark on his forehead, and when the man died the beggar was still there, while the man's three storeys of money were already fought over.

Write a doha where a beggar with a mark on his forehead sits calmly while the rich man inside piles up riches and fears every visitor, showing that the miser's heap falls away but the beggar loses nothing.
beggar, forehead mark, miser's heap
doha about a beggar with a forehead mark and a rich man who hoards
The beggar with the mark on his brow sleeps sound, the rich man tosses on his heap, and the dawn takes the heap but leaves the beggar.

A woman I know saves every rupee, lends nothing to her relatives, and keeps all her ornaments locked away unworn; I'd like a doha on the sadness of a life spent accumulating what is never used or shared.
At the funeral, the sons stood around in silence but I could see them already doing the math on his property; I want a doha that holds that scene.
hoarding, nothing carried
Gathered by sweat and hidden by fear, the heap of wealth stands tall, a monument to a life not lived.
doha for a miser who wont spend a paisa

A diamond sits in the miser's strongbox glittering for no one, and a stone lies by the roadside serving every passerby as a seat; write a doha that shows how hoarded wealth is useless compared with what is freely shared.
My aunt keeps a diamond in a locked drawer she has not opened in twenty years, while a smooth stone by her gate has served the whole street for ages.
The diamond sleeps in darkness, hoarded and unseen, while the roadside stone gives rest to every weary foot.
doha on a diamond and a stone, hoarded riches vs just being useful
diamond, stone, useless hoard
Please write a doha about the money a man gathered over a lifetime of scraping and denying his family, only to leave it with those who will spend it in a month without a second thought.
doha for a miser pls, ur savings stay here when u go
miser's heap, left behind
My father sold his youth for a pension and a pile of savings, and in his last week he told me he wished he had gone on that one trip.
Grain by grain the miser gathered, and one night the gathering was no longer his.

Compose a doha on the foolishness of building up property and bank deposits for tomorrow, as if tomorrow were promised, when in the end all that fortune slips from the grip of the hoarder and falls into other hands.
A relative of mine worked himself sick buying plot after plot and, when he was gone, the plots were sold for less than what he'd sacrificed.
What the hand has gathered, the hand must release; what the heart has hoarded, the heart must leave.
fortune, left behind
write me a doha about someone stacking up riches for no reason
write a doha on the miser who counts his wealth but never lives
Write a doha about a person with a heap of riches too afraid of losing it to sleep soundly or share a meal with a friend, who is eventually parted from all of it while the heap stays behind.
The hoard is a hungry guest at the hoarder's side, consuming the heart that fed it, until it is left to the heirs.
My friend's father still carries his keys everywhere in case someone touches the cash cupboard, even at his own daughter's wedding.
hoarding, lost heap
hoarders leave everything
I'd like a doha for those who pile up money and property to feel safe, pointing out that the heap is the first thing to slip away, and that the safety is imagined while the loss is certain.
Higher and higher he piled his fortune, to be farther from fear, and the height only made the fall greater.
doha pls, about how all that property you hoard doesnt go with you
After my uncle passed, we found stacks of old currency notes in his mattress that were no longer valid, and nobody laughed or cried.
My mother-in-law has spent her entire widowhood guarding ornaments and land deeds from her own children, and when I asked why, she said, someday you will thank me.
doha on greed for property and how it all vanishes in the end

Please write a doha about a person so devoted to accumulating and protecting property that they miss the warmth of family, and who in the end leaves everything to others, taking only the memory of guarding.
hoarded property, gone
Riches are what the miser keeps from all, but death opens every hand and lets them pass to strangers.
The crow circles above the miser's roof, for he too steals the daylight, guarding his hoard from the world it was meant for.
doha with a crow, about rich guys guarding money that gets left behind
Every morning a crow takes bread from our balcony, and I thought of my father's tight fist over his savings that now feeds nobody.
crow, hoarder's money
Write a doha where a crow takes what it needs and flies on, while the hoarder grabs and guards more than he can use, so the crow loses nothing and the hoarder loses everything he guarded.
Into the boat of his fortune the miser loaded everything he owned, and at the other shore even the shroud was left behind.
My father kept loading his business boat with more and more stock, and the day he fell sick, wrapped in a white shroud-like blanket, he asked who would carry it all.
Please compose a doha about a man who loads his fortune onto a boat and sails across life's waters, only to arrive at the far shore in a shroud, with all his riches left aboard.
doha on a boat and a shroud, about hoarded wealth sinking
boat, shroud, hoarded riches
The mirror shows a rich man's face, the dew on the glass shows how brief his hoard, and both clear away by noon.
doha with a mirror and dew, about a rich guy hoarding wealth that disappears
mirror, dew, vanishing hoard
Write a doha where the miser sees himself in a mirror, proud of the property he owns, while a drop of dew on its surface shows how quickly his fortune disappears once he is gone from this world.
Sitting in my late father's study, I looked into the old mirror and noticed dew-like marks on the glass, and thought how his whole life's savings had faded as quickly.
doha pls, about a forehead mark and a cloth sheet over a hoard of riches

Please write a doha about a rich man with a sacred mark on his forehead who covers his piles of savings with a cloth sheet so no eyes may see them, showing no covering saves the heap from falling away.
forehead mark, cloth sheet, hoard
A mark on the brow, a cloth over the hoard; the man looks holy, the hoard sits hidden, and both are taken in time.
My landlord wears a big mark on his forehead on festival days and spreads a cloth sheet over the cupboards where he keeps cash, and then complains about expenses.
boat, gold, hoarder's loss
A family friend who traded gold bought a bigger and bigger boat to carry his stock, and then lost the whole cargo in one storm.
doha with gold on a boat, about wealth lost at the end
Gold is loaded on the boat till it sits low, and then the waves take the gold and the miser both.

Write a doha about a man who piles gold upon a boat, thinking each bar will secure him, but who sinks under its weight and leaves the hoard to the waves, so the miser's heap never reaches the far shore.
need a doha on people who collect so much stuff and cant use it
heaps that fall away
Gathered in darkness, guarded in fear, and scattered at dawn: such is the fate of the heap and the hoarder.
Please write a doha for a man who thinks his bank balance and properties prove his life's worth, and who must learn they pass out of his hands, as they always do, on the day he can no longer count.
When Dadaji's lawyer read the figures out, we all looked at the floor, because he had never once bought himself a coat.
The swan glides on the pond with nothing on its back while the old trader sits counting his hoard and telling his prayer beads, and the world knows which will leave lighter. Please write a doha.
The swan carries nothing and loses nothing, while the old man tells his beads and weighs his fortune, bound to both.
swan, prayer beads, hoarded riches
doha pls, swan and prayer beads, about the rich who hoard
Seeing a swan on the lake near my father's old office, I remembered his prayer beads in one hand and his ledger in the other, and neither could hold him back from leaving.
doha about a miser who wont share and loses everything
The miser stacks his wealth in the dark, and the dark swallows both wealth and miser.
I would like a doha about the person who never gives, never spends, and never rests, only adds and adds to a fortune that will pass entirely into the hands of those who did nothing to earn it.
At school I had a friend whose father owned half the town but gave him pocket money only on Sundays, and later that man's land was divided among five lawsuits.
hoarding, nothing kept
My late uncle's accountant told us the estate is larger than any of us knew, but the man himself lived in two rooms and ate one meal a day.
Please write a doha for a rich person who has collected riches and property for fifty years and has just begun to feel that the heap meant for comfort is, in truth, what falls away from him.
Heaped high is the hoarder's wealth, and heavy upon his heart, until the day it is lifted from him.
heap of riches, gone
doha for rich men who hoard property they will lose
stone, tongue, hoarded riches
doha with a stone and a tongue, about a miser whose savings stay behind
The stone cannot speak yet it outlives the miser's tongue, and the heap he swore to keep is now another's.
My grandfather's tongue was sharp whenever someone asked for a loan, and the same stone gatepost still stands outside his empty property.
Write a doha where a stone and a tongue stand for the miser's unfeeling refusal to share, so that when his tongue falls silent and the heap falls away, only the stone remains as witness.
moneylender, grindstone, heap
The moneylender grinds the poor beneath his grindstone, and gathers a heap that will in time be ground to dust by the same wheel.
doha with a moneylender and a grindstone, about hoarded riches lost at the end
The moneylender in our village grinds out every last paisa from farmers, and everyone knows his fortune will be fought over by his sons after he is gone.

Compose a doha about a moneylender who collects every interest payment with a grindstone's patience, piling up savings and property, only to find that death grinds him down and his hoarded heap falls away.

Write me a doha about how someone can spend years amassing buildings, plots and deposits, believing it is a legacy, when in truth it is just a heap he must leave to others to quarrel over after he is gone.
Rich man, rich man, what do you carry when you leave? Your keys remain, your heap remains, and you go lighter than a child.
My neighbour kept buying flats and never lived in any of them, and when he died, his sons did not even know the address of half.
doha pls about the pointless pile of property
heap left behind
The old grocer in our lane never took a holiday, never gave a discount, and kept every receipt, and at his funeral there were barely ten people but a hundred claimants.
doha about a hoarder whose fortune goes to strangers
The hoarder's fortune is ripe and heavy, and the passing of time shakes it into another's lap.
miser, estate left behind

Please compose a doha showing that the property and savings a man spends his whole life gathering do not leave with him, and that those who live only to hoard end up with no companion except the heap he leaves.
The yogi wears the mark on his forehead and carries nothing, while the rich man carries a vast hoard and ends up carrying nothing too.

Write a doha where a yogi with a mark on his forehead walks lightly through the world, while the hoarder who piled up property and savings must in the end leave the whole heap, showing who is truly richer.
yogi, forehead mark, hoarder
A yogi with a bright mark on his forehead stopped at my landlord's gate for water, and my landlord, who owns eleven properties, could not stop looking at him.
doha about a yogi with a forehead mark vs a rich man hoarding
Our priest wears a bold mark on his forehead and a smile, yet is seen counting donations in a back room and buying plots, and I'd love a doha about that.
priest, forehead mark, hoarding

Please write a doha about a priest with a mark on his forehead who accumulates property and savings under the cover of religion, and the heap he builds will fall away from him as it does for every miser.
doha about a priest hoarding money, forehead mark and all
Marked on the brow with a sign of renunciation, he clutches the heap of the world in hands that must one day open.
Last Diwali my father-in-law refused to buy sweets for the family but bought another plot of land, and I could not tell if I was more angry or sad.

Compose a doha about a man whose entire life is organised around adding to his holdings, who feels poor even with piles of property, and who will leave everything he has gathered to others when his days end.
The hoard whispers to its master: stay, keep me, count me; and the master stays, counting, till the count is over.
doha on greedy hoarding of property that you cant keep
miser's heap
A fly lands on the miser's pile of sweets, which he guards and never eats, and then flies away free; write a doha showing a hoarded heap is useful to no one, not even its guard, and falls away.
A fly was buzzing around the grain my uncle kept stored for years, and I realised it ate more of his savings than he ever allowed himself to.
doha with a fly, about someone who hoards things they never enjoy
The fly alights on the hoarder's heap and tastes it before he does, and flies off lighter than its master.
fly, hoarded heap

Please write a doha about my uncle who saved and saved, wore torn clothes though he owned five properties, and left everything to a cousin he barely knew, showing how riches kept this way are lost to the keeper.
doha on a miser who dies with a fortune he never used
What use the heaped fortune to him who dreads to spend it, for the heap stays and the heart goes empty.
unspent fortune, left behind
My grandfather checked his bank passbook daily till his final week, and when the doctor asked him how he felt, he asked about interest rates.
riches hoarded, riches lost
Write a doha for the man with ten outlets, five flats and three bank accounts who still calls himself poor, whose fortune is a burden he cannot lay down until it is simply taken from his grasp.
doha about hoarding money and losing it all, please
He never trusted banks, so he buried his savings in three places, and after his stroke nobody knew where; I want a doha for that.
Hidden in earth and hidden in fear, the miser's coin lies where no one may use it, nor he.
need a doha for a friend who just keeps piling up property
Heap upon heap the hoarder rises, and with each heap the dark of loss grows longer across his days.
When my wealthy aunt passed, the family found twelve unopened safes full of papers and old coins, each locked with a different key, and nobody even knew her favourite food.
Please write a doha about those who build an ever larger heap of riches and property out of fear of ever being poor, and who find that all they have gathered has to be left behind in the end.
hoard, gone one day
Sitting in the sun outside the bank, I watched an old man count and recount the same bundle of notes, as if it might change what lay ahead.

Write a doha where the sun rises on the hoarder who has already begun counting his property, and sets on the same man still counting, to show that his accumulation does not hold him and does not follow him.
sun, hoarded wealth
The sun climbs over the miser's heap and sets without sharing a ray of its warmth, for the heap is cold and the sun is free.
doha with the sun in it, about a miser and his heap
doha about rich folks hoarding riches that fall away at death pls
Please write a doha for a funeral reading, about the man who piled up land, cash and ornaments as if to take them with him, and who could carry none of it though his hands held the heap tight.
At my uncle's cremation I overheard two cousins whispering about who gets which plot, and he had worked sixty years for that heap.
what the hoarder leaves
Hold the heap tight, O miser, hold it tight, yet the hand that holds it opens by itself at the last.
river, ocean, hoarded riches
Watching my grandfather's fields flood last monsoon, with the river taking the soil toward the ocean, I thought of how he'd hoarded land his whole life and it still would not stay.
doha with a river and an ocean, about riches that people hoard and lose
The river hurries toward the ocean without a coin to its name, while the miser keeps his heap and drowns in it.
Please write a doha where the river runs to the ocean carrying everything away, as a picture of how a miser's riches are swept from him, though he held on to every grain.
